title: Multiplication formula for Hernandez and Leclerc's quivers with potentials

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text cites [LM21, Conjecture 5.1] and also [Pal12] and [XX09] in the introduction, but none of these references appears in the bibliography.

The paper refers to rigid modules over \(\mathcal{A}\) and Ext groups \(\mathrm{Ext}_{\mathcal{A}}^1\), but \(\mathcal{A}\) is the cluster algebra, not the algebra \(A=\mathbb{C}\Gamma^-/J\). Modules and extensions are defined for \(A\), so this is a category/notational error.

The theorem defines \(M^{-\infty} = \bigoplus_{a\in\mathbb{Z}_{<0}} M[a,0]\), but by Definition 2.2 \(M[a,b]\) is defined only for an \(i\)-box, i.e. when \(i_a=i_b\). For \(b=0\), this requires \(i_a=i_0\), which is not true for every negative integer \(a\). Thus the sum is not well-defined as stated.

The proof concludes \(z_1-z_2 \in \mathrm{Hom}_A(M_2, M_{1| W/W'})\), but \(z\) maps \(T'\subset M_1\) to \(W/W'\subset M_2\). The correct space should be \(\mathrm{Hom}_A(T', W/W')\) (or similar), and the notation \(M_{1| W/W'}\) is undefined.
The text says 'Hence, we obtain formula (3.6)' but no equation labeled (3.6) appears in the paper.

The displayed diagram is described as an oriented cycle, but the tikz code shows only a few arrows and does not close a cycle; several vertices have no incident arrows. Therefore the potential \(S\) said to be the sum of 'all these oriented cycles' is not actually represented by the figure.

The paper defines the algebra \(\Pi\), but then repeatedly uses \(\widetilde{\Pi}\)-gmod, \(\Pi(l)=\widetilde{\Pi}/\epsilon^l\widetilde{\Pi}\), and an isomorphism \(\Phi:\widetilde{\Pi}\text{-gmod}\cong A\text{-mod}\) without ever defining \(\widetilde{\Pi}\).

The formula \(\epsilon = \sum_{i\in I} \epsilon_i^{r/d} e_i\) uses an undefined \(d\) and combines it with \(r\), the lacing number. For simply-laced type this is not a well-defined exponent, and \(d\) should presumably be \(d_i\).
The exponent is written as \(\epsilon^{p_a-p_b/2}_i\), which mathematically means \(p_a - (p_b/2)\). It should be \(\epsilon_i^{(p_a-p_b)/2}\). The subscript also changes from \(i_a\) to \(i\).
The theorem writes \(F_{K_{i,r}^{(i)}}\), but the module defined earlier is \(K_{k,r}^{(i)}\), with a positive integer parameter \(k\). \(K_{i,r}^{(i)}\) is not defined.

The proof argues that since \(T\) appears on the right-hand side of the multiplication formula, 'we have \(Y=T\) for all \(Y\)' and then obtains \(F_T=2F_T\). This inference is invalid: the right-hand side may contain several distinct terms, and one term's presence does not force all terms to equal \(T\).

The proof structure is disordered: Lemma 4.4 is stated without proof, then after Theorem 4.5 a second 'Proof' paragraph proves Lemma 4.4. The continuation of Theorem 4.5 uses undefined notation such as \(I_1^{g_i^-}\), \(I_2^{g_i^+}\), \(g'_+\), \(g'_-\) and \(M_{L_1}, M_{L_2}\), and the exact sequences involving these objects are unexplained.
The middle row of the diagram has cokernel \(M_1\), but the restricted submodule \(m(\eta)|_{V'}\) should have quotient \(T'\cong M_1|_{T'}\), not all of \(M_1\).
The proof states \(\mathrm{pr}^{-1}(\eta',V') = \mathbb{P}(E(M_1,M_2) \setminus {}^\perp d')\), but \(d'\) is not defined and the notation \({}^\perp d'\) is not introduced.
